context:
Lock path selection first, then generate the selected implementation TODO.
Do not put both implementations into this item's `work[]`; the local TODO
model cannot represent branch choice without a skipped status. If the
generated TODO needs to differ from the locked spec, cite the Step 5
measurement or Step 0 availability evidence that forced the change.

Path A is significantly simpler if available. Path B is a real software
project (workflow + bot credentials + state machine) and needs fork smoke
testing before enabling on develop.
description:
Deferred queue gate and spec handoff. This TODO does NOT implement a
queue directly. If Step 5 measurement returns BUILD QUEUE, this item
chooses the viable path and creates exactly one follow-up implementation
TODO from the locked spec below:

  - Path A: native GitHub Merge Queue
  - Path B: BenchBox Merge Steward

This shape is intentional. The TODO work-unit graph only supports
`pending`, `in_progress`, and `done`, so mutually exclusive Path A/Path B
implementation units cannot live in the same flat DAG without deadlocking
downstream work. The generated follow-up TODO becomes the executable
implementation item; this gate records the path and prevents re-debating
settled design decisions.

Status starts as Blocked (on Step 5). Three resolution paths:
  - Step 5 -> DO NOT BUILD: this TODO moves to DONE with completion note
    "queue not needed; closed by Step 5 measurement <date>"
  - Step 5 -> BUILD QUEUE: this TODO unblocks, status -> Not Started,
    work units below create the selected implementation TODO
  - Step 5 -> REASSESS: stays Blocked, deps point to next measurement

--- REFRESH 2026-07-23 (dev-loop-step-6-gate-refresh) ---
Re-homed from the retired YAML tracker (_project/TODO/**, removed in the hosted-DB migration) with design content preserved verbatim. Mechanics changes only: the selected-path implementation TODO is created via `todo create` (not a YAML file); validation uses `todo show`/`todo lint` (not validate_todo.py). NEW decision input per _project/planning/ci-failure-reduction-plan.md (WS2/WS9): the w1 BUILD/DO-NOT-BUILD decision must read the CI-failure baseline and 2-week re-measure produced by dev-loop-metrics-ci-failure-baseline-2 (fix-forward pushes/PR, first-pass green rate, fast-lane policy-file touch rate, open-to-merge time) as primary evidence alongside Step 5's measurement window.

anti_patterns.dont: add both Path A and Path B implementation units to this TODO
anti_patterns.why: the flat work DAG cannot mark the unchosen path skipped

anti_patterns.dont: add full matrix to queue-tier CI
anti_patterns.instead: keep queue light, heavy stays nightly
anti_patterns.why: that's exactly the over-engineering Steps 3-5 prevented

anti_patterns.dont: begin queue work without Step 5 saying BUILD
anti_patterns.why: Step 5 might say DO NOT BUILD

anti_patterns.dont: remove develop-post-merge.yml just because the queue runs queue-tier CI
anti_patterns.why: queue-tier and post-merge check different SHAs

anti_patterns.instead: `pull_request_target` is forbidden anywhere in steward workflows
anti_patterns.why: public repos with write-token automation are an exfiltration risk

anti_patterns.dont: use a long-lived PAT for the steward
anti_patterns.why: rotation burden and audit trail are worse than a GitHub App

preserves.behavior: Existing pr-open semantics during deprecation period — do not break in-flight workflows mid-rollout
Heavy validation stays in nightly — do not move it back to the queue path
Only one path implementation TODO exists — no flat-DAG deadlock from mutually exclusive Path A/Path B work
Step 3's lightweight PR-tier CI — the queue does not promote develop to release-grade gating
develop-post-merge.yml safety net from Step 4 remains active even with a queue

verifications.description: Path A or Path B chosen with rationale recorded
verifications.expected: 1 (exit 0; fails until the decision record exists)

verifications.description: Selected-path TODO carries the common queue policy vocabulary
